## Demo target

The demo target is the Upduino 3.1 (iCE40UP5K-SG48), a low-cost board with an onboard 12 MHz oscillator and 8 MB PSRAM. The whole toolchain is open source: Yosys for synthesis, nextpnr-ice40 for place and route, icepack for the bitstream, and icetime for timing analysis.

The demo top module registers the decode on the board clock, so the one-cycle latency and the timing closure are measurable with a real clock:

| Signal | Source | Destination |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| `clk` | pin 20, onboard 12 MHz oscillator | global clock |
| `code[15:0]` | GPIO switch module | decoder input |
| `i[4:0]`, `m[4:0]`, `f[4:0]` | decoder output | LED groups |
| `led_valid` | `~valid`, range check | onboard green LED (negative logic, lights on valid code points) |

Pin constraints are verified against the Upduino v3.1 reference PCF from the icestudio project.

## Place and route flow

```text
synth_demo.ys   -> out/tagma_demo_top.json     (Yosys, iCE40)
nextpnr-ice40   -> out/tagma_demo_top.asc      (place and route, --freq 12)
icepack         -> out/tagma_demo_top.bin      (bitstream)
icetime         -> reports/icetime.txt         (timing report)
```

## Timing results

| Metric | shift-subtract (naive) | multiply-shift (current) |
|--------|------------------------|--------------------------|
| ICESTORM_LC | 177 / 5280 (3%) | 255 / 5280 (4%) |
| SB_IO | 33 / 39 | 33 / 39 |
| SB_GB | 1 / 8 | 1 / 8 |
| Logic levels | 72 | 33 |
| Critical path | 115.90 ns | 59.55 ns |
| Fmax | 8.63 MHz | 16.79 MHz |

The multiply-shift version closes the 12 MHz board clock with margin. The bitstream is generated and the design is ready for board bring-up.

## Board bring-up

The remaining step is physical: program the bitstream, wire a DIP switch module and LED modules to the GPIO pins in the constraint file, and capture the demo. The onboard 8 MB PSRAM also covers the RAM-attached test device question: a chton segment store can be exercised on the same board.

## Second target: iCESugar-Pro (ECP5)

The same RTL builds for the iCESugar-Pro v1.3, an ECP5 LFE5U-25F-6BG256C in a DDR SODIMM module with a 25 MHz crystal. The second device is not there to beat the iCE40 figures. It is there to check that the demo's realization is board data rather than a one-board artifact.

![The board as received: the iCESugar-Pro v1.3 SODIMM module seated in its Ext-Board. Three USB-C ports are visible, one on the module and two on the carrier, and only the module's reaches the ECP5. The carrier breaks the banks out to the labelled headers the demo wiring uses.](../../../_include/icesugar-pro.jpg){#fig-icesugar-pro width=70%}

| Aspect | Upduino 3.1 | iCESugar-Pro v1.3 |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|
| Device | iCE40UP5K-SG48 | ECP5 LFE5U-25F-6BG256C |
| Synthesis | `synth_ice40` | `synth_ecp5` |
| Place and route | `nextpnr-ice40 --up5k --package sg48` | `nextpnr-ecp5 --25k --package CABGA256 --speed 6` |
| Packing | `icepack` | `ecppack` |
| Constraints | PCF | LPF |
| Clock | 12 MHz | 25 MHz |
| Logic | 255 ICESTORM_LC / 5280 | 50 TRELLIS_COMB and 16 TRELLIS_FF / 24,288 |
| I/O | 33 SB_IO / 39 | 33 TRELLIS_IO / 197 |
| Multipliers | not reported | 4 MULT18X18D / 28 |
| Critical path | 59.55 ns | 22.85 ns |
| Fmax | 16.79 MHz | not reported |

The two critical-path figures are not the same quantity. On the iCE40, `icetime` reports the whole placed critical path. On the ECP5, `nextpnr-ecp5` reports the worst cross-domain path, input to register, because the design has no register-to-register path to constrain. They are two device results, recorded as such.

Three board facts decide the constraints. A bank takes one IO standard and nextpnr rejects a mix, so the RGB LED bank at 2.5V holds the only header pin that can use it, and that pin plus the validity pin are `LVCMOS25` while everything else is `LVCMOS33`. Header labels come from the board's pin map. The `code` inputs are pulled up, so an unwired header reads `0xFFFF`, which is invalid, and a switch closes to GND to clear a bit.

The demo drives `led_valid` on ball A12, which is one of the three RGB LED balls and lights on a high level. That is the opposite of the Upduino's negative-logic LED, so the polarity is a top-level parameter instead of a fixed inversion. The vendor README gives the LED balls as the set {A11, A12, B11} and does not assign a colour to each, and the bench observation with only A12 driven reported blue, so the design names its LED signals by function and constrains them by ball.

The module and its Ext-Board each carry a debugger, and only the module's iCELink reaches the ECP5, which is the USB-C port on the module in @fig-icesugar-pro. The Ext-Board's DAPLink answers the CMSIS-DAP handshake and returns `0xffffffff` for every JTAG IDCODE, so the carrier's ports program nothing on the FPGA. The programming path and the wiring table are in `hw/boards/icesugar_pro/README.md`.

## Streaming pipeline

The demo and the streaming design answer different questions. The demo takes one code point from pins and reports a decode, which is the N=1 case. A pipelined decoder takes one code point per clock and never idles, which is the case where a hardware realization can be fed by a stream instead of by a caller. `tagma_decoder_pipe` keeps the arithmetic and the constants of the combinational unit and splits it at the multiplier boundary.

| Stage | Work |
|-------|------|
| 1 | `j = (q4 * 9363) >> 16` |
| 2 | `i = (j * 781) >> 14` |
| 3 | `m = j - 21 * i`, `f = offset - 28 * j` |

The two large constants have no shift-and-add form, so they keep a multiplier each. The two small ones do: 21 = 16 + 4 + 1 and 28 = 32 - 4. Putting the remainders in their own stage therefore replaces two multipliers with adder trees, which shortens the path and removes two `MULT18X18D`.

Latency is three clocks and throughput is one code point per clock. `make sim-pipe` drives the valid range continuously for four sweeps and compares every emitted triple against the combinational decoder, which the other channels already pin at 11,172 of 11,172 points. An exact match at every cycle after the fill carries that evidence to the pipeline.

```text
PASS: 44689 outputs checked over 44692 clocks, 4 full sweeps of the valid space, one code point per clock
```

Place and route reports a clock for this design, which the demo could not produce. `tagma_pipe_top` sources its code from a counter, so its paths run register to register.

| Metric | Pipeline alone | Self-check build |
|--------|----------------|------------------|
| Clock | 25 MHz board oscillator | 40 MHz from the 25 MHz oscillator |
| Fmax, register to register | 127.94 MHz | 58.20 MHz |
| Fmax, reference path | not present | 52.82 MHz |
| TRELLIS_COMB | 51 | 176 |
| TRELLIS_FF | 58 | 154 |
| MULT18X18D | 2 | 5 |
| Bitstream | 582,369 bytes | 582,369 bytes |

The critical path is now stage 1: the counter into the offset subtract, into the multiply by 9363, into `j_q`, at 7.82 ns. The multiplier's 3.93 ns of logic plus the routing around it is the floor for this shape. Registering the offset subtract as its own stage would leave about 6.5 ns, roughly 154 MHz, for a fourth stage and one more clock of latency, which is not a good exchange at the rates this board can supply.

A bitstream that drives unwired header pins proves only that it programmed, so the streaming build carries its own check. `tagma_pipe_check_top` runs the pipeline and the combinational reference from one counter, delays the reference by the pipeline depth, and compares the two triples at every clock. A mismatch latches an indication that stays lit, so a dark error channel after minutes of running is the observation that the two agree at one code point per clock on the device.

| Signal | Ball | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|
| `led_clk` | A11 | blinks at 2.4 Hz while the fast clock runs |
| `led_err` | A12 | lights and latches on any mismatch |
| `led_swept` | B11 | lights once 2^28 clocks have been compared |

The third indication is a rate reading rather than a completion flag, because the comparison saturates and never clears. 2^28 clocks is 6.71 s at 40 MHz and 10.74 s at 25 MHz, so the interval between configuration and that channel lighting separates the two clocks with a stopwatch and no instrument. The PLL is set to 40 MHz rather than the 50 MHz it can also produce because the reference decoder sits in the same clock domain: its path measures 18.9 ns, which is 5.6 percent of margin at 50 MHz and about 32 percent at 40 MHz. The split that raised the pipeline to 127.94 MHz did not move that path, because it is the reference that is binding here.

The first build of the check compared against `28'hFFFFFF`, six hex digits against a 28-bit register. The comparison type-checked and the design built, but the count saturated at 2^24 clocks and the readout fired after 0.42 s instead of 6.71 s. A literal and a register that disagree in width still compare, so an elapsed-time claim has to be checked against the constant rather than against the declared width.

A second silence is device-wide. `code` originally started at `16'hAC00` so that the first comparison cycles would already be in the valid range. The ECP5 global set and reset implements only all-zero initialisation, so `synth_ecp5` emitted the register with no `INIT` parameter and warned about nothing: the device powers up at zero. A four-line counter initialized to `4'b1010` reproduces the same silence. The counter is now written to start at zero, which is what the silicon does, and the first pass reaches the valid range on its own. Any register here initialized to a pattern other than all-zeroes gets zeroes on this device and no diagnostic.
